# Knowledge Ops

Curated by Skill Harbor: an operations skill for running a multi-layered knowledge system. It covers ingesting documents, conversations, and notes into structured storage; syncing knowledge across layers (local files, MCP memory, vector stores, Supabase, Git repos); deduplicating and organizing what accumulates; and retrieving across the whole system when you ask "what do I know about X". Its workspace model is opinionated in a useful way: code work lives in real cloned repos, active execution context lives in GitHub, Linear, and repo-local working-context files, broader human-facing notes live in a non-repo archive folder, and durable cross-machine memory belongs in the knowledge base rather than a shadow workspace. Trigger phrases include "save this to KB", "sync knowledge", and "ingest this". By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; works best when the storage layers it orchestrates are actually connected; sync across systems needs credentials you manage yourself. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
